EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
1.	ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICIES
At Dyno Nobel Inc, Graham, Kentucky, (Dyno Nobel) we are committed to operating and maintaining all our processes (especially those using hazardous substances) in a safe and responsible manner. We use a combination of accidental release prevention programs and emergency response planning to help ensure the safety of our employees and the public as well as protection of the environment. This summary is presented in response to the requirements of the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) under Title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations, Part 68 (40 CFR 68), and Section 112(r) of the Clean Air Act. 
2.	 STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES
Dyno Nobel is an explosives manufacturing facility. The facility is subject to the RMP rule due to the storage of nitric acid (conc 80% or greater), a regulated toxic substance, above the threshold quantities. 
3.	GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION STEPS
Our company and our employees are committed to management systems which set the way we do business, and we have specific accountabilities and controls to ensure that we are meeting our own high standards for accident prevention. We maintain several programs to help prevent accidental releases and provide safe operation. These programs address accidental release prevention measures required by EPA, process safety management (PSM) requirements from the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), and notification requirements of EPA's Emergency Response and Community Right-to-Know regulations. 
Employee Participation
Dyno Nobel has developed an employee participation program. All process safety information, process hazard analysis (PHA) results, recommendations, and action items, incident investigations, compliance audits, operating procedures, emergency response plan, and records of management of change are available to the opera

ting personnel.
Process Hazard Analysis and Process Safety Information
The facility utilizes the What If/Checklist Combined and cause mapping PHA methodologies. The PHA identified the following potential major hazards: toxic release, fire, explosion, runaway reaction, overpressurization, corrosion, overfilling, contamination, and equipment failure. The facility utilizes process controls including vents, relief vents, check valves, scrubbers, manual shutoffs, automatic shutoffs, interlocks, alarms and procedures, backup pump, grounding equipment, and a quench system to prevent or limit releases. 
Dyno Nobel keeps a variety of technical documents that are used to help maintain safe operation of the facility. The facility also maintains technical documents that provide information about the design and construction of process equipment. 
Operating Procedures and Training
Dyno Nobel maintains written procedures that address process operations. The facility has developed and implemented a training program for all employees involved in facility operations. 
Contractors
The contractor safety procedures establish minimum guidelines and activities to ensure that the contractor's employees follow safe work practices and procedures. The procedure includes a contractor screening process and hazard awareness, safety, and emergency procedures training.
Pre-Startup Safety Reviews
Dyno Nobel conducts a pre-startup safety review (PSSR) for facility modification that requires a change in the process safety information. The purpose of the PSSR is to ensure that safety features, procedures, personnel, and the equipment are appropriately prepared for startup prior to placing the equipment into service.
Mechanical Integrity
The facility's mechanical integrity program includes written procedures, training, and regular inspections and equipment testing procedures to maintain piping systems, relief systems, emergency shutdown systems, and controls in a safe operating condition. 
Management o

f Change
The facility's management of change (MOC) program reviews all proposed changes to process chemicals, technology, equipment, procedures, materials, and design conditions prior to implementation of the change. Changes are reviewed to ensure that adequate controls are in place to manage any new hazards, and to verify that existing controls have not been compromised by a process change. 
Incident Investigation
Dyno Nobel has procedures to promptly investigate any incident that has resulted in or could result in the release of a regulated substance. The procedure establishes the minimum guidelines and activities of the incident investigation program to reduce the likelihood of repetitive occurrences of events which could lead to catastrophic releases. Investigations will be undertaken to identify the situation leading to the incident as well as any corrective actions to prevent a similar release in the future.
Compliance Audits
The facility conducts audits of the provisions of RMP to verify that procedures and practices developed under the standard are adequate and are being followed. The audits include a review of documentation and process safety information, inspection of the physical facilities, and interviews with all levels of facility personnel.
These individual elements of our prevention program work together to prevent accidental chemical releases. FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
We keep records for all accidental chemical releases that occur at our facility. Dyno Nobel Inc has not had any incidents covered by the RMP rule in the past five (5) years.
4.	EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM
We maintain a site-specific Emergency Action Plan, which consolidates the various federal, state, and local regulatory requirements for emergency response planning. Our program provides essential planning and training for effectively protecting workers, the public, and the environment during emergency situations. The purpose of the emergency action plan is to protect workers and publ

ic safety as well as the environment. The emergency action plan addresses aspects of emergency response, including proper first aid and medical treatment for exposures, evacuation plans and accounting for personnel after an evacuation, notification of local emergency response agencies and the public if a release occurs, and post-incident cleanup and decontamination requirements. Employees receive training in these procedures as necessary to perform their specific emergency response duties. We work with the local fire department and emergency responders to ensure the proper execution of our plan. Furthermore, we have established coordination for emergency response and made available copies of our plan to local and county fire departments, medical facilities, police, and public works.
5.	PLANNED FACILITY ENHANCEMENTS
The Dyno Nobel facility has been designed and constructed to meet existing construction and process safety requirements.  We regularly review and audit the safety of our manufacturing processes to minimize the potential for accidents and chemical releases, with modifications being made as needed. We will continue to evaluate and implement changes as necessary to improve safety at the facility.
